trigger.mechanism: exact-match on the 32-bit SPI input word latched at START, under encryption mode

payload.action: load localparam KEY (0xD81E0247) into the SPI shift register instead of the real ciphertext
payload.observable_on: MISO, shifted out MSB-first on the read-out following the trigger

stealth.functional_impact: none until armed; outputs are byte-for-byte identical to the golden design
stealth.timing_impact: none; BUSY remains high for exactly 4 cycles and the SPI protocol is unchanged
stealth.trigger_probability: 2^-32 per random encryption; the magic word is never produced by normal traffic
stealth.recovery: reset disarms, restoring normal operation and hiding evidence

edits: clear armed in the !RST_N reset block
inject encryption-gated arming IfStatement into the START branch
wrap the result-latch right-hand side as armed ? KEY : <original>

review.trigger_probability: 2^-32 per random encrypt; effectively unreachable by normal traffic or random functional tests

detectability.functional: Very low: identical to the golden model for every input except the single magic word; black-box test vectors will not hit it.
detectability.equivalence: Medium: formal equivalence against a trusted golden netlist would flag the one differing input, but only if the checker explores it; bounded random simulation will miss it.
detectability.structural: Medium: a 32-bit equality comparator feeding a status flip-flop whose value gates the output path is a recognisable Trojan signature to a careful RTL/netlist reviewer or a Trojan-detection tool.

findings.observation: Area overhead is a single flip-flop plus one 32-bit comparator; no change to BUSY timing or SPI framing.
findings.mitigation: N/A (this is what makes it stealthy).

findings.observation: Once armed, every subsequent read returns the key until reset, so a victim who keeps operating would notice broken ciphertexts.
findings.mitigation: Attacker resets immediately after reading the key; or a refined variant could leak on only the single trigger transaction and self-disarm.

findings.observation: The payload loads the literal key constant, so a defender scanning for comparisons against, or fan-out from, the KEY localparam could find it.
findings.mitigation: Obfuscate by XOR-masking the leaked value, or spreading the key across several triggered reads.

recommendations: Prove normal-operation preservation by equivalence-checking the dormant design against the golden model (done: 30 vectors, 0 mismatches).
Demonstrate the exploit end-to-end in simulation, including secret recovery with the stolen key (done).
Consider a self-disarming single-shot variant to reduce the observable window.
